workingTitle: Dwarf galaxies kept only a tenth of the oxygen their stars made
freshness: Peer-reviewed paper published in The Astrophysical Journal on November 2, 2026; selected within the preferred 15-day window.
coreFacts: The GLOW team measured oxygen production, distribution, and retention in 37 gas-rich, star-forming dwarf galaxies within 6 megaparsecs.
The galaxies span stellar masses from about 10^6.5 to 10^9.5 solar masses and retained 3.8% to 24.8% of the oxygen their stars produced, with a mean of 10.7% and a sample standard deviation of 5.1%.
About 80% of the sample, 29 of 37 galaxies, retained no more than 15% of their produced oxygen.
Most of the retained oxygen is in interstellar gas, with smaller amounts in stars, stellar remnants, and dust.
Hydrodynamical simulations reproduce the mass-metallicity relation but predict higher oxygen retention than the observations show.
caveats: The retained fractions combine several measurements and assumptions, including stellar yields, stellar population histories, gas masses, oxygen abundances, dust depletion, and alpha-to-iron ratios.
The sample contains nearby gas-rich, star-forming dwarf galaxies and should not be generalized without qualification to every kind of dwarf galaxy.
Ultraviolet absorption studies constrain only part of the circumgalactic oxygen reservoir and require uncertain ionization corrections.
The study does not establish whether most missing oxygen remains in the galaxies' circumgalactic surroundings or escaped into intergalactic space.
Galactic winds are the leading explanation for oxygen removal, but the study reconstructs the cumulative budget rather than directly observing every past outflow.
